system.name: DSF (Definition-Specific Familiarity)
system.one_liner: Study of how LLM priors and user task definitions interact in zero-shot toxicity annotation: familiarity, error rescue and misaligned definitions.

content.variant_note: a shared Setup column fans out by dashed arrows to three colour-framed research-question rows, each with the question, the manipulated item, a sketch plot and findings bullets
content.argues: Definition alignment, not text memorisation, predicts annotation accuracy; prompts rescue only about a third of errors; misaligned definitions hurt accuracy but not confidence.
content.subject: A grey zero-shot annotation setup feeding three research-question rows, each with a manipulated definition, a trend sketch and findings.

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each research question its own colour-framed row with identical slots (question, manipulated input, sketch of the expected trend, findings bullets), and one shared setup column that fans out to every row by dashed arrows.
lessons.suits: Analysis or evaluation papers with several research questions probing one shared setup, whose answers fit a trend sketch and two bullets.

evidence: We investigate this tension through three research questions (Figure 1):
RQ1 tests whether task familiarity correlates with performance, contrasting definition alignment (Definition-Specific Familiarity; DSF) with text memorization metrics
Insets summarize the main empirical findings for each question.

summary: The paper studies how model-internalized priors interact with user-provided task definitions when LLMs annotate toxic text zero-shot. Figure 1 is a study overview. A grey Setup column shows the annotation setup: an input text with its instruction, an LLM box with a robot icon, and a red-tinted wrong prediction 'not toxic'. Dashed arrows fan from the LLM to three rounded rows framed in blue, green and brown for Research Questions 1 to 3. Each row holds the question, the manipulated item (familiarity measures, an aligned definition, a misaligned definition), a rounded frame with a tick-free sketch plot of the trend, and a Findings column of coloured bullets (definition alignment predicts accuracy; about a third of errors are rescued; misaligned definitions keep confidence but hurt performance).
